text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:

- Coalition passes tax reform measures in parliament as opposition votes against bill. Tax rates and solidarity tax level would be cut sharply in two steps while tax loopholes closed and indirect taxes raised.

- Deutsche Telekom will sell a 25 percent stake to Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau in two tranches in 1997 and 1998, Telekom chairman Ron Sommer tells annual shareholder meeting. He said the shares will be then sold to strategic investors at market rates.
- Federal accounting office criticises high pay for top managers for the planned telecommunications and post control agencies.
- Telekom holds key for digital TV. After deal between Bertelsmann and Kirch on digital pay TV there appears to be an avenue now open for resolving the technical access to the digital net.

- Handelsblatt economic barometer for eastern Germany shows that the recovery in the east continued in June. The index rises to 6.5 percent in June compared to 6.2 percemtn a month earlier and reaches its highest level in 18 months.
- German trade federation (BDI) warns against false goals for tax reform and negative effects on economy. --Bonn Newsroom +49 228 260 97160
